No evidence found in the supplied material of a separate named-customer rumor, patent catalyst, or acquisition lead; the stock move looks primarily like a post-earnings/order re-rating plus technical momentum

VPG reported Fiscal 2026 Q1 results on 2026-05-13, with orders exceeding $100 million and revenue of $84.4 million, up 17.6% year over year; management highlighted strong demand in semiconductor equipment, data centers, avionics, military and space, plus bookings up 25% sequentially.

The same release indicated expanding momentum on the bottom line: the recent quarter cited in market coverage showed adjusted EPS of $0.07 versus $0.21 expected and a weaker Q1 guide around $77 million, but the stock’s much larger multi-week move appears to be driven by a sharp re-rating after the later 2026-05-13 earnings/update and order surge rather than the earlier miss alone.

Market commentary and coverage also point to the stock breaking into new highs after the order and revenue acceleration, with the move amplified by very high relative strength (RSI mktcap percentile 98) and a volume spike on 2026-05-13.
